summary: Ensho Kobayashi is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He has been affiliated with Hanazono University, where he is attested as professor in 1988 and professor emeritus in 2026.
Ensho Nasu is a scholar of Buddhist studies who completed a PhD at Ryukoku University under Esho Mikogami (attested 1996). In 2007, he was attested as a visiting researcher at Ryukoku University.

Enshu Kurumiya is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied under Yukio Sakamoto, Ensho Kanakura, and Yosho Nomura, and earned his PhD at the Australian National University under Jan Willem de Jong in 1974. He later served as professor at Rissho University (attested 1981–1985).

Entai Tomomatsu (1895–1973) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Keio University around 1920–1923. He held a post at Taisho University and founded the Publishing Association of Abhidharmakosa-vyakhya.

Erberto Lo Bue (1946–2022) specialized in Tibetology and history and archaeology. He earned his PhD from SOAS University of London (~1976–1981) and held posts at the University of Milan (~1993) and the University of Bologna (~2002–2017).

Eric David Mortensen is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. He completed his PhD at Harvard University (attested 2003) under Leonard van der Kuijp, Michael Witzel, and Kimberley C. Patton, and also studied under Chongren He, Xiaoxun He, Zhiben He, Xi Aniu, and Xuewen He.

Eric George Hart (1878–1946) was an Indology and linguistics scholar educated at Wellington College and Victoria College, Jersey. He served as Professor of Arabic, Persian and Hindustani and Reader of Indian History at Trinity College Dublin from 1926 to 1938.
Eric Haruki Swanson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He has held a post at Loyola Marymount University and served as a Senior Visiting Scholar at Stanford University (attested 2026).
Eric Huntington is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under the supervision of Gary A. Tubb.

Eric J. Sharpe (1933–2000) was an Indology and religious studies scholar. Educated at Manchester and Uppsala under Samuel Brandon and Bengt Sundkler, he held posts at Lancaster, Sydney (First Chair of Religious Studies, 1977–1996), and Uppsala (1978–1981).

Eric M. Greene is a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar who completed his PhD at UC Berkeley under Robert H. Sharf. He has held faculty posts at San Francisco State University (2023) and Yale University (attested 2017–2026).

Eric P. Hamp (1920–2019) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Amherst College and Harvard University under Joshua Whatmough. He held academic posts at the University of Michigan (~1950–1953) and the University of Chicago (~1953–1991).

Eric Stephen Goodell is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned MAs from the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies and the University of Virginia (attested 2012), where he studied under Paul Groner.

Eric Thomas Stokes (1924–1981) was a historian who earned his PhD at Cambridge under Thomas Spear. He held posts at the universities of Malaya, Bristol, and Zimbabwe, before serving as Smuts Professor at Cambridge (1970–1981).
Eric Villalobos is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. He has been affiliated with Emory University's Graduate Division of Religion, where he is attested as a doctoral student in 2026.

Erica Baffelli is a scholar of Japanology and religious studies who studied under Massimo Raveri. She held a post at the University of Otago (attested 2015) and serves as Professor in Japanese Studies at the University of Manchester (attested 2016–2026).
Erica Biagetti is a scholar in Indology, linguistics, and computational studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Pavia by 2021 and holds a post there.

Erich Arno Lehmann (1901–1984) worked in Indology and religious studies, earning a Dr.Theol. at Leipzig (~1945–1947). He served on the faculties of Leipzig, Jena, and Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg, where he was Dean of the Theological Faculty (1950–1966).

Erich Berneker (1874–1937) was a linguist who earned his PhD at Leipzig under August Leskien. He taught at Humboldt University, the German University in Prague, and held chairs in Slavistics at the universities of Breslau (1909–1911) and Munich (1911).

Erich Frauwallner (1898–1974) was an Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy scholar who completed his PhD at the University of Vienna under Bernhard Geiger. He held multiple academic posts at Vienna from 1928 to 1964 and founded the Wiener Zeitschrift für die Kunde Süd- und Ostasiens.
